evidence_conflicts: Ammonia is called liquid ammonia in the Experimental prose, while Figure 1 labels NH3(aq). The formulation is not resolved and no ammonia concentration is inferred.
Figure 3 calls as-prepared A amorphous; the Figure 5 annealing-time discussion starts from 4 nm. The latter is retained only in its time-series context, not assigned as the as-prepared SEM/XRD size.
The 600 °C time series is distinct from the 24 h temperature series; no temperatures or time ticks are converted to invented individual tabulated measurements.
Source calls its microscopy SEM and names 2000FX JEOL. The method/instrument wording is retained without silently substituting TEM.
The 50 µm agglomerate size and resistance unit Ω are visually read from the printed page; cached OCR misreads these as mm and V.
Text summarizes A as 20 nm at 60 h, whereas the two Figure 5 reflection traces differ visually. Textual 20 nm is not a precise value for both reflections.
Text gives approximately 70 m²/g at 300 °C for both populations. Figure 7 B is visually higher; no plot-derived replacement is made.
Figure 4 axis says mass loss (%) while curves descend from 100. Only the explicit text water-loss values are extracted; the axis is not repaired.
remaining_gaps: The supplied main-article scope passed independent source review; missing quantities and sample crosswalk limits below remain unresolved. No publication or exact-coordinate training approval is implied.
Physical aliquot IDs and SEM/XRD/TG/Auger crosswalk are not reported; links use the named A/B preparation population only.
No atomic coordinates, complete lattice constants, measured particle-size distribution or gas-sensing response is provided.
Heating/cooling ramps and specimen masses are unreported. Cited separate cryosol methods were not read to fill gaps.
SnCl4·5H2O mass, water volume, initial concentration, ammonia amount/concentration/addition duration, stirring rate, centrifuge force/time, wash volumes/count and yield are unreported.

Alpha-stannic-acid charge, NaOH volume, total stannate volume, resin identity/capacity/total mass/cycle count/separation are unreported. Freeze-drying pressure, duration, exact freezing time/rate and full schedule are absent.
source_notes: Liquid-nitrogen freezing and ice templating are the authors’ explanation for platelets. Particle-uniformity/heat-stability reasoning invokes Lifshits and Slezov; Figure 8 is theoretical, not a measured distribution.
Authors associate the estimated activation energy with literature oxygen vacancies and anticipate gas-sensor benefits. Neither vacancy concentration nor gas-sensing performance is measured here.

items.title: Powder A: conventional precipitation and 100 °C drying
items.summary: Dissolve the stated but unquantified precursor charge in deionized water in an ice bath. The bath temperature is not numerically reported. Slowly add ammonia to the stirred solution until alpha-stannic-acid precipitation is complete. Preserve the prose/Figure 1 formulation ambiguity. Centrifuge and wash with deionized water until the AgNO3 test indicates no chloride. The analytical test does not imply adding AgNO3 to the retained bulk precipitate. Dry the washed precipitate. Drying atmosphere is not specified.

items.title: Powder B: cation exchange and freeze drying
items.summary: Dissolve the stated but unquantified precursor charge in deionized water in an ice bath. The bath temperature is not numerically reported. Slowly add ammonia to the stirred solution until alpha-stannic-acid precipitation is complete. Preserve the prose/Figure 1 formulation ambiguity. Figure 1 branches from precipitated alpha-stannic acid to sodium stannate. No 100 °C drying step is inherited from A and no shared physical batch is asserted. Dilute the sodium stannate solution; final volume is unreported. Add small resin portions, age 15 min after each cycle to approach hydrolytic equilibrium, and monitor pH. The resulting colloid has pH 6.5. No total number of cycles or resin-removal operation is specified. Freeze-dry the colloid to friable powder. The Results discuss liquid-nitrogen freezing as the platelet-template explanation; the operational freezing/drying schedule is not supplied.
